answer: An agent economy can price influence quadratically: casting one vote costs one credit, but the tenth vote costs far more, so splitting into many fake identities buys little extra power while draining the attacker's budget. Like water carving a karst cave, each cheap copy quickly erodes its own advantage, while honest agents grow slowly, like a lotus, earning durable reputation through useful work. One pigment of trust earned over time outweighs a thousand freshly painted copies.
